author: Laurens Kuiper <laurens@ducklabs.com>
message:
Partial aggregate pushdown gives the new lower aggregate the estimate of
the aggregate above the join. That estimate is often the join estimate
itself, and it can exceed the lower aggregate's own input. The build
side optimizer then sees a huge aggregate and builds the other side of
the join instead.

Example, TPC-H q10 at SF3000:
- The lower `GROUP BY o_custkey` has 63M groups but was estimated at
1385M rows.
- So all 450M customer rows were built without a runtime filter.
- The top join took 156 instead of 24 thread-seconds.

The lower aggregate's estimate is now capped at both its input estimate
and the product of the current domains of its groups. The cap never
raises an estimate.

At SF1000 the only plan change is the build side of one join in TPC-DS
q74. The q10 case shows up with filter selectivity sampling (#28664),
whose estimates make the original estimate larger than the input.
subject: Cap the estimate of a pushed down partial aggregate by its input and group domains (#28716)
title: Cap the estimate of a pushed down partial aggregate by its input and group domains

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
This is yet another PR in a series of PR's that aim to step-by-step make
our bound expression/operator tree immutable.

# Motivation

Immutable bound expressions can be shared instead of deep-copied, so the
binder and optimizer can reuse the same subtree in several places (and
trivially cache or hash it). It also unlocks future development on the
optimizer as it makes optimizer passes easier and safer to reason about:
a rewrite produces a new tree that can be evaluated against other
candidates independently rather than mutating nodes that other plan
alternatives or code may still hold references to.

# Changes

## Mutable setters removed

- `BoundConstantExpression`: removed SetValue/TakeValue, added
WithValue().
- `BoundReferenceExpression`: removed IndexMutable, added WithIndex().
- `BoundLambdaRefExpression`: removed its three mutable accessors, which
had no callers.
- `BoundDefaultExpression`: the one site that retyped it in place now
creates a new node.

Also a bunch of other call sites have been changed to replace the
expression in its slot, instead of mutating it. The largest change being
in `move_constants.cpp`. Even though doing this replacement is slightly
more costly than just mutating in-place, these are all operations on
leaf expressions, so there is no quadratic subtree copy cost.

## ExpressionIterator::PreorderReplace

This is a new helper function to visit expressions in pre-order
traversal, with the main change being that the callback receives a
`const unique_ptr<Expression>` and is expected to return a _new_
`unique_ptr<Expression>` when making a change (instead of mutating in
place) or return `nullptr` on no change.

Internally this just calls `::VisitReplace` and mutates anyway - but the
idea is that this will help in migrating more expressions to be
immutable - and eventually replace `::VisitReplace` entirely.

## Alias/QueryLocation passed on construction

Expressions currently have two mutable setters,
`SetAlias`/`SetQueryLocation`, which are used in lots of places. In
theory we could replace these with immutable "wither"-style
copy-and-modify helpers like `WithAlias`/`WithQueryLocation`, but given
that we use these a lot on nested expressions, its not really feasible
to force a full copy right now while copies are still expensive (and not
always supported, e.g. in `BoundSubqueryExpression`.

This PR attempts to avoid calling these setters at all in some cases by
instead drilling down and passing the alias/query location directly to
the constructor of whatever expression we are creating whenever we are
somewhat close to the construction site.

There are still a lot of `SetAlias`/`SetQueryLocation` calls left,
particularly in the binder, and some will not be possible to remove at
all until copying becomes cheap (e.g. in
macro/expression-returning-function binding), so this will remain a
work-in-progress.

# Future work

- Finish removing the mutable setters in `BoundColumnRefExpression`. A
bunch of calls remain in optimizer passes and helpers such as
`ColumnBindingReplacer`, `RemoveUnusedColumns`, the CSE optimizer, etc
etc. Most of them hold references to expressions and mutate them later,
so they need some restructuring before the accessors can be deleted.

- Remove the remaining base-class setters on bound expressions.
`SetAlias`, `SetQueryLocation`, `SetReturnType` etc. The biggest
remaining piece is `ExpressionBinder::Bind`, which needs to stop
stamping alias and location after the fact.

- Verification stats should move to a side table and not be part of the
`Expression` base class at all

- Switch to a `shared_ptr<const Expression>` once all mutators are gone
subject: Make more bound expressions more immutable (#28704)

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
Follow-up to #28574 and #28571.

Moves 12 more settings from hand-written
`SetGlobal`/`SetLocal`/`ResetGlobal`/`ResetLocal`/`GetSetting` to
generic settings (`default_value` in `settings.json`), using `OnSet`
where the setting has validation or side effects. `OnSet` also runs on
`RESET` (with `info.is_reset`), so side effects stay in sync.

**Fully generic, readers use `Settings::Get`, the
`DBConfigOptions`/`ClientConfig` field is removed**
- `debug_force_mbedtls_unsafe` (`OnSet` autoloads httpfs when disabling
with encrypted databases attached)
- `debug_delta_only_variant_encoding_enabled` (`OnSet` rejects every
change)
- `debug_force_variant_shredding` (validated in `OnSet`, parsed in
`DBConfig::GetForceVariantShredding`; default `INVALID` as before)
- `allocator_bulk_deallocation_flush_threshold` (`OnSet` pushes to the
buffer pool)
- `custom_user_agent` (`OnSet` appends to the previous value, refuses
changes once the database runs)
- `profiling_coverage` (now `ENUM<ProfilingCoverage>`)
- `profiling_output` (validated against the profiler format in `OnSet`)
- `extension_directories` (`VARCHAR[]`, on top of the list support from
#28574)

**Generic, with `OnSet` pushing into state that other code reads
directly**
- `debug_verification_mode`: static
`DBConfigOptions::global_verification_mode`, read without a config in
the vector code
- `disabled_optimizers`, `disabled_compression_methods`: state lives in
`DBConfig` / the compression function set; the stored value is the
normalized list
- `checkpoint_threshold`: `options.checkpoint_wal_size` is read on every
commit, so it stays a parsed cache

Other changes
- `DBConfig::ResetOption` runs the callback for generic options too (as
`RESET` already did), so resetting through the config API keeps side
effects in sync.
- `CALL enable_profiling(...)` sets `profiling_coverage` /
`profiling_output` through `PhysicalSet::SetVariable` so `OnSet`
validation still applies.
- `Settings::Set` skips `OnSet`, so tests that previously assigned the
removed fields now call it directly.
- New test `test/sql/settings/generic_migrated_settings.test`.

Not converted, with the reason, so the remaining ones are easier to pick
off:
- Computed defaults: `threads`, `async_threads`, `max_memory`,
`temp_directory`, `max_temp_directory_size`, `operator_memory_limit`,
`max_streaming_buffer_size`, `standard_vector_size`,
`storage_compatibility_version`, `secret_directory`, `http_proxy`
(environment fallback).
- Value is derived from other mutable state, so a stored value would go
stale: `allowed_paths` (attaching adds paths), `allowed_directories`,
`allowed_configs`, `disabled_filesystems`, `http_client_pool_capacity`
(reports the live capacity), the logging settings (`LogManager`), the
secret settings (virtual `SecretManager`), `enable_profiling`,
`profiling_mode`.
- Coupled to each other: `schema`, `search_path`, `current_dialect`,
`active_grammar_extensions`, `default_grammar_extensions`.
- `access_mode` is set directly on `DBConfigOptions` by the shell, tests
and the open path.
- `profiling_renderer_settings` is a `MAP`, which `Settings::Get` does
not support yet.

Tested on a RelWithDebInfo build: `test/sql/settings/*`, `[api]`,
`[wal]`, `test/sql/pragma/profiling/*`, `test/sql/function/variant/*`
and `test/sql/storage/compression/*` pass.
subject: Migrate more settings to generic settings (#28700)

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
hunk_contexts: class AttachedDatabase : public CatalogEntry, public enable_shared_from_this<Att
message:
Prototype: invalidate a single attached database after an unrecoverable
error, instead of invalidating the whole database instance. The
invalidated database rejects all use until it is `DETACH`ed; reattaching
it recovers from its files, and the instance, the default database and
sibling attachments stay usable.

This builds on the existing scoped invalidation for checkpoint failures
(`AttachedDatabase::Invalidate`, per-database `ValidChecker`) and
generalizes it.

### Changes
- `AttachedDatabase::Invalidate(cause, error)` replaces the
checkpoint-only `Invalidate(reason)`. The message is now `Database "x"
has been invalidated because <cause>. Detach and reattach it before
using it again. Original error: ...`. The checkpoint message is
unchanged.
- `AttachedDatabase::SupportsScopedInvalidation()` is false for the
system, temp and initial (default) databases. For those, `Invalidate`
escalates to instance-wide invalidation, matching the existing
checkpoint behaviour, because they cannot be detached.
- `AttachedDatabase::ScopeFatalError(ErrorData)`:
`MetaTransaction::Commit`/`Rollback` pass each per-database
commit/rollback error through it. A `FATAL` error from a database that
can be detached stays fatal, but gets the database name attached as
extra info (`Exception::INVALIDATED_DATABASE_KEY`). This covers a real
EIO fsync failure (`FatalException("fsync failed!")`),
rollback-after-failed-commit failures, index removal failures during
commit, etc.
- The invalidation sites in `ClientContext`/`QueryResult` call the new
`ValidChecker::Invalidate(DatabaseInstance &, const ErrorData &)`. It
invalidates the attached database named in the error, or the whole
instance if there is none. `ErrorData::Merge` keeps the name only when
every fatal error names the same database.
- Sites that invalidated the instance directly for a single database's
failure now go through `AttachedDatabase::Invalidate`:
  - a failed commit revert (`DuckTransaction::Commit`)
  - a failed append revert (`LocalStorage::Flush`)
- a failed post-commit WAL sync
(`DuckTransactionManager::CommitTransaction`)
  - the `before_wal_flush` debug crash
- `WriteAheadLog::SyncUpTo` invalidates a scoped database when its WAL
sync fails. That WAL can never be synced again, so the database is
unusable until reopened. The default database keeps its current
behaviour.

### Test
`test/sql/storage/attach/attach_invalidation_commit.test` covers:
- a WAL fsync failure on an attached database
- a commit plus revert failure on an attached database
- a fatal mid-commit crash on an attached database

For each one it checks that the sibling, the default database and the
instance stay usable, and that detach/reattach recovers. It also checks
that the same failure on the default database still invalidates the
instance.

Ran locally (reldebug + FORCE_ASSERT): the new test,
`test/sql/storage/attach/*`, `wal/*`, `concurrent_wal/*` (including
slow), `test/sql/transactions/*`, the commit/append-revert failure
tests, and the `[storage]` group. All passed.

### Not covered yet / open questions
- Fatal errors raised during query execution (not commit/rollback), e.g.
ART corruption, still invalidate the instance: at that point we don't
know which database they belong to.
- Read-side corruption (`DataCorruptionException` on checksum mismatch)
still only fails the query. Should it invalidate the attached database?
- No user-visible state yet. A column in `duckdb_databases()` showing
invalidation could be added.
subject: Scope unrecoverable errors in an attached database to that database (#28650)

author: Laurens Kuiper <laurens@ducklabs.com>
message:
The statistics propagator derives filters from inner/semi join bounds,
but previously lost them when the binder cast a column to the common
comparison type. For example, TPC-DS Q72 compares
`CAST(inv_quantity_on_hand AS BIGINT) < cs_quantity`, so the known
maximum of `cs_quantity` did not bound the inventory scan.

Derive these filters through invertible numeric casts using the existing
cast capability checks. This includes integer and decimal widening,
precision-safe conversions to floating point, and FLOAT to DOUBLE.
Convert each bound back with the built-in cast; inclusive bounds remain
conservative when conversion rounds, and the original join comparison
remains in place. Unsupported conversions and TRY_CAST are skipped, and
registered cast overrides retain their semantics. This stays within the
numeric types supported by join-statistics tightening.

The author's original integral-cast benchmark reported Q72 at SF1000
improving from 56 s to 1.5 s, and at SF3000 inventory input dropping
from 1.445B to about 139M rows. Those measurements predate the broader
numeric coverage.

Validation: the join-statistics suite (55 cases), cast optimizer suite
(9 cases), and three cast-pushdown tests pass with assertions and
float-cast-overflow sanitization enabled. All 540 differential queries
across 15 numeric type pairs match the previous PR head and
optimizer-disabled execution, including rounding, precision boundaries,
NaN, infinities, and NULLs. A 1M-row decimal-inequality microbenchmark
improves from a 99 ms median to 21 ms with identical results; IMDB and
TPC-DS were not rerun for this follow-up.
subject: Derive join statistics filters through invertible numeric casts (#28717)
title: Derive join statistics filters through invertible numeric casts

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
A plan that DuckDB versions before 2.0 serialized for a struct with a
`count(*)` field in a correlated subquery, for example `SELECT x,
(SELECT {'y': t.y, 'n': count(*), 'b': t.b} FROM o WHERE o.k = t.x) FROM
t`, no longer deserializes: "Failed to find function
struct_pack(VARCHAR,BIGINT,BOOLEAN)", which "takes no positional
arguments".

Plans written before v2.0.0 carry the argument names of `struct_pack`
only as the aliases of its arguments, and `RestoreNamesFromAliases`
takes the names from the trailing aliases, stopping at the first
argument without one. v1.x decorrelation (`RewriteCountAggregates`)
replaces the reference to the count with `CASE WHEN x IS NULL THEN 0
ELSE x END` without keeping the reference's alias, so that argument has
none and the arguments before it stay positional.

The fields of the recorded STRUCT return type are the argument names of
a v1.x `struct_pack`, so for a function that takes only keyword
arguments and returns a STRUCT with one field per argument, this takes
the names from the return type. The new `struct_pack_count_subquery`
case was serialized by v1.5.6.

This is a regression for plans written by v1.x, could it get the
`backport v2.0-cyanoptera` label?
subject: Read v1.x plans of struct_pack whose field lost its alias (#28740)
title: Read v1.x plans of struct_pack whose field lost its alias

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
A plan that DuckDB versions before 2.0 serialized for `approx_quantile`
over a DECIMAL column no longer deserializes: "Failed to find function
approx_quantile(BIGINT)", or another integer type, depending on the
DECIMAL's width.

In v1.x, `BindApproxQuantileDecimal` erased the quantile argument and
then replaced the whole function with the one for the DECIMAL's physical
type, which dropped `original_arguments`, so these plans record only the
shortened argument list. v1.x read them through a fallback in
`AggregateFunctionSet::GetFunctionByArguments` that took the first
overload whose leading parameters had the recorded types; #25991 removed
it. The existing `erased_arg_approx_quantile` case does not catch this,
because its DECIMAL call does carry original arguments.

For an aggregate in a plan written before v2.0.0 without original
arguments, when no overload matches, this selects the first overload
whose leading parameter types and return type match the plan and
completes the argument list with its remaining parameters. Matching the
return type keeps a scalar call from picking a list overload. The new
`erased_arg_approx_quantile_decimal` case was serialized by v1.5.6.

This is a regression for plans written by v1.x, could it get the
`backport v2.0-cyanoptera` label?
subject: Read v1.x plans of approx_quantile over DECIMAL (#28737)
title: Read v1.x plans of approx_quantile over DECIMAL

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
Projection placement moved each comparison of a column that other
expressions of the same projection also read, such as the `d_moy = 1` ..
`d_moy = 12` conditions of TPC-DS q66, below the joins onto the small
side. That frees no input column. It only adds one column per expression
that the joins have to carry.

When the small side is the build side of a hash join, these columns come
back as a global dictionary that every thread reads. The CASE
expressions above then contend on its shared validity buffer. At SF3000,
q66 took 1.19 s instead of 0.62 s.

With this PR, projection placement no longer moves an expression with a
heuristic cost of at most 20 (for example, a comparison of a numeric
column with a constant), unless moving it frees one of its inputs.

Of the 99 TPC-DS queries, only q66 changes plan. It only changes with
filter selectivity sampling (#28664): with sampling, q66 is otherwise
33% slower at SF1000 and SF3000, and this PR removes that regression.
subject: Do not move cheap projections below joins when their inputs stay needed (#28715)
title: Do not move cheap projections below joins when their inputs stay needed

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
Extension options write their default into the global user settings when
they are registered. `RESET` also writes it back, globally or as the
session value. This is unlike built-in options keep their default on the
option and resolve it at lookup time. So for extension options:

- An option the user never set looks the same as one the user explicitly
set to its default: `TryGetCurrentUserSetting` finds a value either way.
There's no way to tell.
- `RESET x` pins the default as the session value instead of falling
back to the global value.
- For an option without a default, `RESET x` leaves NULL as the session
value, so `TryGetCurrentSetting` reports it as set.

This PR resolves extension option defaults the way built-in ones are
resolved: registration no longer stores the default,
`TryGetCurrentSetting` falls back to it, and `RESET` / `RESET GLOBAL`
clear the setting.
subject: Keep extension option defaults out of the user settings (#28714)

author: Laurens Kuiper <laurens@ducklabs.com>
message:
Fixes #28511.

A recursive CTE whose step joins the working table to several
recursion-independent tables can run out of memory on 2.x where 1.5.6
finishes in milliseconds. In the issue's reprex, `powers` and `params`
are joined to each other on the group id alone before the frontier is
joined in, a per-group cross product growing with K^2 while the result
stays at 60,000 rows. The join-order optimizer plans the recursive
member against estimates with no reliable relation to the executed row
counts: the recursive scan is estimated at 327,868 rows against 60,000
actual, and the step at about 2e12, so a product of two independent
inputs looks cheap and is bounded by neither input nor the frontier. The
plan change dates back to #22211.

An earlier version of this PR rejected every recursion-independent pair
whose output exceeds both inputs. Review by @lnkuiper produced a
counterexample that breaks that rule: two 100-row tables joining to
5,000 rows answer a 100,000-row frontier 300x faster than the forced
frontier expansion. His prototype replaced the rejection with a
memory-aware cost, and its structure is the first commit here, with
credit: the join-order cost becomes work plus peak build memory, build
sizes are tracked per plan with retained builds of repeatable
independent inputs separated from transient ones, and per-relation
recursive properties shared with the build/probe-side policy replace
ad-hoc checks.

The memory cost alone is not enough. Below the memory budget it reduces
to the plain work model over the same unreliable estimates, which
re-picks the bad plan at K=10 - the prototype's K=10 time matches the
unmodified base exactly. The second commit keeps one narrow guard on
top: a recursion-independent pair whose estimated output exceeds both
inputs and the recursive frontier estimate is rejected. The
counterexample's 5,000-row build stays admitted far below its
100,000-row frontier, while the issue's 4M-row-estimated product is
rejected and the member joins onto the frontier spine, where every build
is bounded by an input.

The guard has one refinement, contributed by @lnkuiper on this branch: a
pair above the frontier estimate is still admitted when a single later
join predicate needs columns from both inputs on one side, such as a key
assembled as `a.x * 100 + b.y`. Splitting such a build across the
frontier spine cannot evaluate that key as a hash condition. The issue's
shape stays rejected, since its conditions are plain column equalities
with each side in one relation. His change also accounts for retained
builds inside independent subtrees and keeps the recursive properties
flowing when memory costing is disabled, with regressions covering
compound keys assembled from two and three inputs under both
enumerators. The issue-shape measurements are unchanged by it.

Final query of the issue's reprex and the review counterexample,
reldebug builds with the base 2 GB figure from a release build, medians
of 3+ hot runs:

| | base (main) | first version | review prototype | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| review counterexample | 0.004 s | 1.200 s | 0.004 s | 0.003 s |
| issue reprex K=30, 2 GB | 9.2 s | 0.140 s | 0.083 s | 0.147 s |
| issue reprex K=10 | 0.236 s | 0.075 s | 0.235 s | 0.059 s |

The v2.0.0 build the issue reports runs out of memory on the K=30
reprex, current main survives it 60x slower than this PR. The remaining
gap to the prototype at K=30 comes from a retained independent build
whose cost amortizes across iterations. Single-execution estimates carry
no iteration count, so no estimate-space rule can admit it without
readmitting the K=10 product. Recovering such plans is the recursive
cardinality estimates follow-up named in review.

The protections keep the issue's full-scale result and the assertion
that the per-group product is never built, pin a reducing independent
join as still allowed, and assert the counterexample's independent build
is chosen, with plan pins guarded against storage-dependent statistics.
subject: Cost recursive-member joins by peak build memory and bound independent joins by the frontier estimate (#28521)

author: Laurens Kuiper <laurens@ducklabs.com>
message:
`ParensTableRef` accepted any table reference in parentheses, so `FROM
(CALL query('SELECT 42'))` parsed as a table named `CALL` with alias
`query` and column alias `"SELECT 42"`, failing at bind time with "Table
with name CALL does not exist!". Other unreserved keywords (`PRAGMA`,
`EXECUTE`, ...) hit the same path.

This restricts parenthesized table references to joins, as in v1.5, so
these are syntax errors again. `ParensTableRef` is packrat-memoized to
keep nested parentheses linear.
subject: Only allow joins inside parenthesized table references (#28648)

author: Laurens Kuiper <laurens@ducklabs.com>
message:
#24058 made every in-place `UPDATE ... FROM` register its target row ids
in one shared set under a global lock, which serializes large updates.
That caused a regression as described here:
https://github.com/duckdblabs/exaforce/issues/49. This PR restores the
in-place path. A target matched by several source rows is again updated,
counted and returned once per match. As discussed in
https://github.com/duckdblabs/duckdb-internal/issues/11537, this trades
correctness for performance, and a proper fix will be made for `2.1`
subject: Revert #24058: UPDATE ... FROM / MERGE multi-match deduplication (#28701)

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
A plan serialized by v1.x with a `MERGE INTO ... WHEN MATCHED THEN
UPDATE SET col = DEFAULT` on a table of a catalog other than DuckDB's
own, such as Iceberg or DuckLake, fails on 2.0 with "INTERNAL Error:
Attempting to initialize state of expression of unknown type!".

v1.x bound DEFAULT as a placeholder (BoundDefaultExpression), which the
update operator replaced by the default of the column when it ran. Since
#23033 the binder resolves defaults, but plans that still contain the
placeholder are supported: PhysicalUpdate resolves it. Since #25228 the
actions of other catalogs are planned through their regular
INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE planning. The SET expressions of an update action
are now evaluated in a projection before the catalog's update operator,
so the placeholder ends up in the projection, where it can't be
evaluated.

This PR replaces the placeholder with the bound default of its column
before the projection. It mirrors the deprecated branch that #25228 kept
for the insert action, which fills in the defaults of omitted columns of
v1.x plans.

Could this still be backported to v2.0?
subject: Resolve SET col = DEFAULT of MERGE plans from before v2.0 (#28739)
title: Resolve SET col = DEFAULT of MERGE plans from before v2.0

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
hunk_contexts: static auto CV2TableScanColumns(const CV2TableFunctionData &bind_data, const Tab
message:
Stable C++ API additions needed to port
[duckdb-orc](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb-orc) to the stable C++ API
(see the duckdb-orc PR). All additions are unstable, and kept to a
minimum.

## Table functions
- `AddVirtualColumn(FILE_ROW_NUMBER)` (+ `VIRTUAL_COLUMN_START` index
convention): a single-file function can expose `file_row_number`
(`duckdb_v2_table_function_add_virtual_column`).
- `SetMetricsCallback` / `MetricsInput::SetMetric(name, value)` (C:
`duckdb_v2_table_function_metrics_set`): report operator metrics of the
scan by the name `tracked_metrics` uses: `operator.rows_scanned`,
`operator.row_groups_scanned`, `operator.total_row_groups_to_scan`,
`operator.bytes_scanned`. Any other name is rejected.
- `BoundReference` is exposed as `BOUND_COLUMN_REF` in the expression
API.

## Filters, without new C functions
A scan that wants to prune with the query's filters (e.g. skip ORC
stripes by their statistics) uses the existing filter pushdown callback.
The callback only runs at optimization time, and the optimizer only
offers the predicates to the multi-file wrapper, so a function wrapped
in a `MultiFileFunction` never saw them. Now a function that has both a
filter pushdown callback and projection pushdown is offered the
single-column predicates once more when a scan starts, just before the
global init callback, with the bind data of the file being scanned. The
engine applies these predicates to the rows the function produces itself
(accepting has no effect), so the function can only prune. No new C API
function is needed for this.

## Statistics (on top of #28140)
- `Stats::GetValue()` / `Stats::SetValue(Value)`: the C++ wrappers of
`duckdb_v2_stats_get_value` / `duckdb_v2_stats_set_value`, so a stats
callback can report min/max/NULL-ness as a STRUCT value.
- The multi-file wrapper of a table function now reads the statistics of
its files through `statistics_extended` only (what the C API registers),
instead of the plain `statistics` callback. The single-file Parquet
reader is converted to the extended form. Before, a C API/C++ API table
function wrapped in a multi-file function never reported statistics for
its files.

## Tests
- `[cpp_api]` tests for virtual columns, metrics, the filters offered

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
`ReadSingleParquetFileBind` in
`extension/parquet/read_single_parquet_file.cpp` has a local named
`interface`. The Windows COM headers define `interface` as a macro
(`#define interface struct` in `combaseapi.h`, pulled in by `windows.h`
without `WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN`), so with that macro in effect the
declaration becomes `ParquetMultiFileInfo struct;` and clang-cl fails
with `declaration of anonymous struct must be a definition`.

The parquet extension's translation units do see `windows.h` (thrift's
`PlatformSocket.h` includes `winsock2.h`), and main compiles today only
because `duckdb/common/windows_undefs.hpp` happens to be included again,
via `null_value.hpp`, after the thrift headers, which undefines the
macro before the local is reached. On a branch that changed the include
graph `null_value.hpp` was first included earlier, the `#undef` no
longer ran after `windows.h`, and the Windows (64 Bit) job failed on
this line. Renaming the local to `file_info` removes the dependency on
include order; no behaviour change.

Note: this PR was generated by an AI coding agent and reviewed by the
author.
subject: Rename a Parquet bind local called interface, Windows headers define it as a macro (#28734)

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
The new extension build (`DUCKDB_NEW_EXTENSION_BUILD`) commits each
extension patch on top of the pinned commit, so
`duckdb_extension_generate_version` stamped the hash of a local patch
commit. Builds that go through FetchContent patch the working tree
without committing and stamp the pin, so linux_amd64 reported a
different `extension_version` than every other platform for any patched
extension.

- `duckdb_extension_generate_version` now skips commits whose subject is
a patch filename (`<name>.patch`, what `sync_out_of_tree_extensions.py`
writes) and reads the hash and tag from the commit below them.
- Unpatched checkouts are unaffected: the walk stops at HEAD.
- `scripts/ci/test_sync_out_of_tree_extensions.py` gets a test for the
stamped version.

With the three httpfs patches on main, configure now reports `Load
extension 'httpfs' from extension/external/httpfs @ a2485c0fd2`, the pin
in `.github/config/extensions/httpfs.cmake`.
subject: Stamp patched out-of-tree extensions with their pinned commit (#28658)

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
Follow up to #28605.

#28605 made `repeatable` default to whether the seed is set on both the
write and the read side. On the write side that leaves the property out
for every REPEATABLE sample, and v2.0.0 would read a missing
`repeatable` as false, then run it as a non-repeatable sample. For
example, v2.0.0 would return different sample when reading a view with
`TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI (25 PERCENT) REPEATABLE (42)` written with
#28605.

This PR always writes `repeatable` when serializing for storage version
v2.0.0 or later (v2.0.0 itself wrote it only when true), so v2.0.0 reads
REPEATABLE samples as repeatable and a seeded sample that is not
repeatable still reads back as not repeatable. The seed-based default
stays on the read side, so plans and views from v1.x, which never have
the property, still read as repeatable when they have a seed.

The serialization generator gave a `bool` with only a
`deserialize_default` the implicit `false` write default, so it skipped
writing it when false. Properties with only a `deserialize_default` are
now always written, as the generator's comment on `deserialize_default`
already describes.
subject: Keep REPEATABLE samples readable by v2.0.0 (#28640)

author: Laurens Kuiper <laurens@ducklabs.com>
hunk_contexts: static inline data_ptr_t InsertRowToEntry(atomic<ht_entry_t> &entry, const data_
message:
### Problem

`test/issues/general/test_27205.test` returns too few rows from a hash
join on the Windows 32-bit CI job, losing a varying number of build-side
rows between runs (one run returned 15733800 instead of 15734000,
another 15732800). It appeared after #28622 lowered the threshold for
building a join hash table in parallel to 65536 rows: the failing
query's build side has 78670 rows and the 4-core Windows runner now
inserts into the table from several threads.

The parallel insert loop reads entries with
`atomic<ht_entry_t>::load(std::memory_order_acquire)`. `ht_entry_t` is 8
bytes; on a 32-bit target the MSVC STL implements that load with
`__iso_volatile_load64`, which clang-cl (the compiler of the Windows
32-bit job) lowers to two 32-bit `mov`s. A thread can therefore observe
a half-written entry: the new pointer in the low half with the old salt
still zero in the high half. It treats the entry as occupied with a
non-matching salt, probes on, and starts a second chain for a key that
already has one; the probe later finds only the first chain and the rows
in the second one are silently dropped. With libstdc++ the same load is
a single `fildll`, which is why 32-bit Linux builds do not show the
problem; 64-bit targets load 8 bytes atomically.

### Fix

`LoadEntryConcurrent` reads an entry via
`compare_exchange_strong(expected, expected)` when a pointer is narrower
than an entry, which is a single `lock cmpxchg8b` and leaves the entry
unchanged; 64-bit targets keep the plain acquire load. The two loads on
the parallel insert path (the probe loop in `InsertHashesLoop<true>` and
the expected-entry load in `InsertRowToEntry<true, false>`) use it. The
single-threaded path is unchanged.

### Verification

- The torn load was confirmed by compiling the MSVC STL's 8-byte atomic
load with `clang++ --target=i686-pc-windows-msvc -O2 -S`: the load is
two 32-bit moves, the store likewise.
- 64-bit release build: `test_27205.test`, `test/sql/join/*` (205),
`test/issues/general/*` (130) and `test/sql/parallelism/*` (79) pass.
- 32-bit Linux build with gcc on an x86 machine: `test_27205.test`
passes 5/5 at 4 threads with and without the fix (libstdc++ loads
atomically), `test/sql/join/*` passes apart from an out-of-memory in an
ASOF slow test that fails identically without the fix (32-bit address
space; not run by CI).
- The Windows 32-bit job of this PR is the real check; main's nightly
passed that job once on 392cee07532, which is consistent with a race.

Note: this PR was generated by an AI coding agent and reviewed by the
author.
subject: Read join hash table entries atomically while other threads insert (#28682)
title: Read join hash table entries atomically while other threads insert

hunk_contexts: bool DBConfig::CanAccessFile(const string &input_path, FileType type, optional_p
message:
## Remote path traversal

Remote paths could pass an allowed-directory prefix check and then use
`..` to access a different location. When external access is disabled,
we now reject these segments before checking the allowlists, including
encoded dots and separators. Extension downloads now use the same check.
Local filesystem canonicalization is unchanged.

## Secret scope matching

A secret scoped to a host or bucket could match a different host or
bucket with the same prefix. When a scope ends at the host or bucket,
require an exact match or a `/` boundary. This prevents `@`-based host
changes and longer host or bucket names from matching the scope, while
preserving file/key-prefix and scheme-wide scopes.

This changes compatibility: host/bucket-name prefixes such as
`s3://bucket-` no longer match `s3://bucket-1/...`. URLs with an
explicit port also need that port in the scope, including default ports
such as `:443`. These uses now require explicit scope entries.

Fixes: <https://github.com/duckdblabs/duckdb-internal/issues/11901>
Fixes: <https://github.com/duckdblabs/duckdb-internal/issues/11899>
Fixes: <https://github.com/duckdblabs/duckdb-internal/issues/11896>
subject: Fix remote path traversal and secret scope boundaries (#28684)

message:
Follow-up to #28471 and #28594: another pass over the remaining
`Value::DefaultCastAs` uses, threading a `Context &` where one is
already at hand so user-registered casts apply.

- **`list_value`**: the fallback path casts with the expression's
`Context` (`ExpressionState::GetContext()`, now mandatory since #28594).
- **parquet `FIELD_IDS`**: `FieldID::GetFieldIDs` takes a `Context &`
and casts the field ids with it.

in `GetCardinality`.

- Statistics (parquet statistics/metadata, variant stats in
`expression_filter`): must match runtime values, same reasoning as

(`IsDefaultCast` is asserted on).

author: Laurens Kuiper <laurens@ducklabs.com>
message:
Supersedes #28381, fixes #28372 in a simpler way.

The PEG transformer merged `(A UNION B) UNION C` into one N-ary UNION
node, so the inner set operation never resolved its own result type and
`87::INTEGER` was cast straight to `VARCHAR` instead of through
`DOUBLE`.

`TransformSelectSetOpChain` now only merges into the N-ary nodes it
builds itself. A chain's first operand can only be a set operation when
it was written in parentheses (no other
`SelectAtom` alternative produces one), so such an operand stays nested
and the binder stages the cast through it. Unparenthesized chains are
unchanged and still become a single N-ary node.
subject: Union staged type casts operand (#28692)

static bool CanUseCompressedProbe(const HashJoinGlobalSinkState &sink, const vec
message:
Integer joins with a compact build-key range can now use direct lookup
within the normal hash join. Bounds come from the rows actually built,
so eligibility does not depend on statistics or runtime-filter pushdown.

`PerfectHashJoinTable` owns the integer bounds and lookup storage;
`JoinHashTable` selects and builds the representation; the existing scan
structure handles predicates, join semantics and output. This replaces
the separate perfect-hash executor.

* SEMI, ANTI and uncorrelated MARK joins can use a compact membership
bitmap, including duplicate keys and NULL-safe equality.
* Row directories retain duplicate chains, additional
non-equality/residual predicates, and outer, SINGLE and right membership
join semantics.
* Eligible unique INNER joins retain dictionary output. Dictionary
conversion is skipped when the estimated probe is smaller than the
actual build.
* Large, scattered bitmap probes use adaptive prefetching through the
shared prefetch helper. Small batches and sampled hot-word patterns
retain the scalar lookup.
* External joins, unsupported key types, multiple equality keys and
ranges that exceed the allocation budget use the ordinary hash table.
Lookup storage is capped at 8 MiB and constrained by its cost relative
to the build/hash directory. Correlated MARK joins retain row-based
processing.

The tests cover backend activation, NULLs, integer boundaries,
dictionary and compressed vectors, duplicate chains, residual
predicates, runtime filters, recursive reuse and external fallback.

Release note: scalar subqueries now detect duplicate qualifying rows
farther along a hash-join chain and consistently raise “More than one
row returned by a subquery used as an expression” with the default
setting. This also fixes the ordinary hash path, including VARCHAR keys.
The behavior fix is a separate commit;
`scalar_subquery_error_on_multiple_rows=false` retains the permissive
behavior.

Compared with main `46257b1490e452ed59f1061cc0fc9c6e90841720`, using
SF10, eight physical cores/threads, an 8 GB memory limit, one warmup and
five interleaved samples in persistent CLIs:

| Suite | Architecture | Main total (ms) | PR total (ms) | Time change |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TPC-H, 22 queries | ARM | 2,160 | 2,140 | -0.9% |
| TPC-H, 22 queries | x86 | 2,368 | 2,343 | -1.1% |
| TPC-DS, 99 queries | ARM | 8,872 | 8,484 | -4.4% |
| TPC-DS, 99 queries | x86 | 10,250 | 9,611 | -6.2% |

Totals sum the per-query medians; lower is better. Q22 improves from 49
to 45 ms on ARM and 59 to 54 ms on x86. Runtime logs confirm bitmap SEMI
and integer MARK lookups in its default plan. All 121 base/PR results
agree on both architectures. Q78 has a rounded-ratio difference from the
stored reference (`0.97` versus `0.98`) shared by main and this PR.

Some individual queries remain slower: TPC-DS Q14/Q22 on x86 were
5.5%/4.0% slower in the suite and about 2% slower in separate 11-sample
checks. Comparing the merge commit with the dictionary safeguard changed
those recheck medians by at most 1 ms, with identical backend
activation.

The small-probe safeguard was measured separately with 500k retained
build rows and one probe row: 10→8 ms / 14→10 ms at one thread on
ARM/x86, and 8→4 ms / 9→4 ms at eight threads. Larger probes were
unchanged. With normal optimizer reductions, the reviewer's original
example remains about 1 ms on both versions.

Native ARM and x86 each pass 25 hash-join cases / 2,162 assertions. The
separate ARM assertion build with `STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE=512` passes the
same cases. The focused tests also pass 39 configurations, including
statement verification, serializer verification, forced external
execution and `delim_join_as_cte`.

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
Fixes #27759. This is #28623 by Yannick Welsch (his two commits
unchanged), plus one commit of extra tests.

### The fix (from #28623)

When the right side of a dependent join is a CTE that does not use the
domain, the CTE is moved above the join. Unless the join was a SINGLE
join with an uncorrelated left side, decorrelation then restarted the
whole join, so the left side was prepared twice. With a LIST correlation
(no duplicate elimination) that adds a second `row_number()` window
under the same table index, which fails with `INTERNAL Error:
Conflicting or cyclic column binding replacement`. The trigger repro
from #27759 goes the same way. The fix continues with the right side
after moving the CTE up, which is the path the SINGLE case already used.

### Also fixes a wrong result

The restart also gave silently wrong results for a CTE inside a nested
lateral join. On main this returns `2497 3666`, while the correct answer
(the same query written as a plain join) is `250 367`:

```sql
CREATE TABLE q AS SELECT i % 3 AS s, i % 4 AS k FROM range(200) t(i);
CREATE TABLE o AS SELECT i AS x, i % 3 AS g FROM range(10) t(i);
SELECT count(*), sum(n.k)
FROM o, LATERAL (SELECT * FROM (SELECT o.x) p,
                 LATERAL (WITH st(k) AS (VALUES (1), (2))
                          SELECT q.k FROM q WHERE q.k IN (SELECT k FROM st) AND q.s = o.g AND q.k < p.x)) n;
```

### Plan impact

I compared optimized plans on main and on this branch for LATERAL,
EXISTS / NOT EXISTS, IN, `> ANY`, scalar, LEFT LATERAL,
LIMIT-in-LATERAL, LIST, nested and stacked-CTE queries. They match,
except:
- the LIST and nested-lateral queries, which are the fixed bugs;
- two stacked independent CTEs (`WITH a AS (...), b AS (...)`). The
restart used to move both CTEs above the join; now only the first one
moves. `b` stays on the join's right side, but `PushDownCTE` leaves its
definition free of the domain, so it is still computed once. Results and
runtime were the same (about 2.05s at 20k x 2M rows).

### Extra tests in this PR

- the nested lateral wrong-result query above
- the two stacked independent CTEs
- removed `PRAGMA enable_verification` from the new test file

Could this get the `backport v2.0-cyanoptera` label? It is a v2.0
regression.
subject: Fix wrong results and "Conflicting or cyclic column binding replacement" when a lateral join reads a CTE (#28698)
title: Fix wrong results and "Conflicting or cyclic column binding replacement" when a lateral join reads a CTE

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
Fixes #27940.

The report’s query (a hash join of positions to rates, a CASE whose ELSE
branch is the build-side column fx_rate, and a selective filter on the
result) fails with INTERNAL "dict-surviving cache: global dictionary
column 1 changed identity after being seeded for dictionary caching" and
invalidates the database. The same happens with threads=1, with IF(...),
or with the branches swapped. With SET enable_caching_operators=false
the result is 31. The second reproduction in the report (CAST(JSON AS
VARCHAR)) already works on main, since the cache matches global
dictionaries by id.

The dictionary-aware operator cache (AppendToCache in
src/execution/physical_operator.cpp) pins a column’s global dictionary
on the first small chunk and accumulates selection indices for the
following chunks. If a later chunk carried a different dictionary or
none, a global dictionary threw, on the assumption that a producer emits
the same global dictionary for its whole lifetime. An expression above
the producer breaks that assumption: the CASE returns the join’s
dictionary vector unchanged for a chunk in which every row takes the
ELSE branch, a constant for an all-THEN chunk, and a flat vector for a
mixed chunk, so the filter’s cache saw the dictionary for some chunks
only. The hash join build already handles this on its side:
BuildColumnIsComputed treats a projection-computed column as one that
may arrive as a dictionary for some chunks only and does not narrow it.

The fix removes the throw and demotes the column to flat (materialize
the rows cached so far, then append flat). The cache has had that
demotion path for a rotating non-global dictionary, but only global
dictionaries are ever seeded, so it was never taken before. A flat
column is what the sinks receive without the cache. Other operators
forward a global dictionary for some chunks only as well (an external
hash join’s spilled probe rows come back flat, a cross product forwards
a column as a reference or as a constant depending on chunk sizes), so
the early check produced false positives for legitimate shapes. The hash
join build’s own checks still protect its row store.

Added test/sql/join/hash_join/dict_cache_computed_column.test (55
assertions): the report’s tables and query, IF, the swapped CASE,
sum/min/max of the demoted column, a GROUP BY sink, a VARCHAR dictionary
column, a switch between two global dictionaries from two joins, window
and ORDER BY LIMIT sinks, and a 500k-row case with threads=1 where two
dictionary columns go through several cache cycles and only one is
demoted and re-seeded. Expected values come from runs with
enable_caching_operators=false.

Verified on join (incl. hash_join), cte, aggregate, optimizer, filter,
parallelism, window, types/nested, subquery, projection and types/string
suites. The new test was run under disable_optimizer, verify_fetch_row,
force_external, vector_size_512, verify_serializer, shredded_vector,
verify_statement_prepare, verify_statement_copy and
disable_caching_operators.
subject: Demote a global dictionary column in the operator cache when its dictionary changes (#27979)
title: Demote a global dictionary column in the operator cache when its dictionary changes

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
Fixes https://github.com/duckdblabs/duckdb-internal/issues/11173

DETACH closes the database once `use_count() == 1`. But `use_count()` is
a relaxed load, so it doesn't synchronize with threads that already
dropped their reference without `close_lock`, e.g. a scanner that got
the database from `GetDatabases()`. TSan then reports a race between
their reads (`GetCatalog()`) and `Cleanup()`.

This PR copies our reference and drops the copy right before `Close()`:
- The decrement is acq_rel, so it synchronizes with all earlier
decrements of the counter.
- Dropping a copy rather than `attached_db` itself keeps the count at 1,
so we still close with the `checkpoint_on_detach` action instead of
through the destructor.
- This relies on `shared_ptr` decrements being acq_rel even when they
don't reach zero. That holds for all three standard libraries DuckDB
builds with (libstdc++, libc++, MSVC STL). An acquire fence would also
work, but TSan doesn't model fences.

The added test has a thread take a reference, read the catalog and drop
it, then runs DETACH. Without the fix it fails under TSan on every run.
subject: Synchronize with dropped references before closing a detached database (#28696)
title: Synchronize with dropped references before closing a detached database

author: Laurens Kuiper <laurens@ducklabs.com>
message:
`ColumnReader::block`, the buffer holding each page's decompressed data,
was previously allocated with an `Allocator` and was always kept pinned.

This moves `block` onto the buffer manager
(`BlockHandle`/`BufferHandle`), pinning it only around each vector's
read and unpinning it in between. `ByteBuffer` was changed to use an
offset-based cursor instead of an absolute pointer. Further, every
decoder that caches a pointer into `block` (dictionary, RLE,
delta-binary-packed, byte-stream-split) now rebases itself against the
new address after each re-pin.

One buffer was deliberately left on `Allocator`: the bloom filter built
while writing a dictionary page. It's short-lived and never re-pinned,
so buffer-manager tracking would only add overhead there with no
eviction benefit.

I ran a small benchmark locally, no speed regression, and it now keeps
working once memory gets tight enough that main just runs out of memory.

Also includes a small unrelated build fix in `expression_binder.cpp` I
hit along the way.

This looks like a lot of changes, but a lot of the changes are because
many of the functions were renamed for formatting reasons (ie. `inc()`
-> `Inc()`).
subject: Allow Pinning/Unpinning of ColumnReader::block (#25570)

message:
Push runtime join filters through STRUCT field extraction without
changing the scan's existing projection.
The filter input is an owned bound expression over that projected value:
- a scan of `s.nested.a` uses `#0`, a scan of `s.nested` uses the
residual field extraction,
- and a scan of `s` retains both extractions.

Copying the bound expression preserves operation order and original
function/cast bind data. The custom-cast regression binds offset 7 and
requires input 10 to produce 17; reconstructing an INTEGER-to-BIGINT
cast from types alone would produce 10. Cast-error/NULL handling,
storage-order restrictions, and eligibility remain conservative. This
change does not expand LIST/MAP/VARIANT eligibility.

The single commit contains six implementation files, three regression
files, and one test registration. Its source tree is identical to
evaluated head `ae4c3c323bc2dc0aa62622cfa706f2c938762dba`, based on
verified upstream main `392cee07532cad39193661814ff35309b7437b1f`. It
uses upstream's new default-cast input factory.

Focused validation through my notebook MCP, using a freshly built CLI
whose source ID and binary hashes were checked:

| Query output | Scan projection | Row groups with runtime filtering |
Disabled-filter control |
|---|---|---|---|
| Field | `s.nested.a` | 1/10 | 10/10 |
| Retained substruct | `s.nested` | 1/10 | 10/10 |
| Retained full struct | `s` | 1/10 | 10/10 |

Results and scan projections match the same-binary disabled-filter
controls.

- NULL/equality semantics, ordinary CAST overflow, TRY_CAST, six
cast/projection combinations,
- and three storage-order controls pass. Ordinary narrowing CAST retains
upstream [#28641](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28641)'s
conservative all-row-group scan;
- no change is included to restore the older pruning behavior. No
cross-version timing claim is made.

Permanent regressions pass:
- Custom bound-cast data, 6 assertions; STRUCT joins, 71 assertions;
projected scan bindings, 15 assertions.
- Formatting and diff whitespace checks pass. The focused notebook is
`pr-28265-focused-atomic.ipynb`;
- Recorded evidence retains source/executable identities, raw plans,
controls, and initial failed assumptions.
- Broad local suites were not restarted. CI for this new commit will be
reported separately.

Addresses the [upstream
review](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28506#pullrequestreview-5824002321).
duckdb/duckdb#28265.

AI-assisted implementation and evaluation.

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
Since `AT TIME ZONE` on a `TIMESTAMP_NS` returns a `TIMESTAMPTZ_NS`,
comparing the result with a `TIMESTAMPTZ` fails to bind, while
`TIMESTAMP_NS` and `TIMESTAMP` compare fine:

```sql
SELECT (TIMESTAMP_NS '2026-10-12 12:34:56.123456789' AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') < now();
-- Binder Error: Cannot compare values of type TIMESTAMPTZ_NS and type TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE - an explicit cast is required
```

The same happens for `BETWEEN`, `COALESCE`, `IN` and list literals that
mix the two. They combine the types through an implicit cast in one
direction, and `CastRules::ImplicitCast` has no rule for a
`TIMESTAMP_TZ` source, so neither direction is allowed.

This allows `TIMESTAMP_TZ` to `TIMESTAMP_TZ_NS`, as `TIMESTAMP` already
casts implicitly to `TIMESTAMP_NS`, so the microsecond side is cast up.
On #28039 the different ranges of the two types came up as the reason
against this cast. `TIMESTAMP` and `TIMESTAMP_NS` differ in the same
way, and a `TIMESTAMPTZ` outside the nanosecond range now fails with the
same "Could not convert Timestamp to higher precision" that a
`TIMESTAMP` gets today. The cast also lets a `TIMESTAMPTZ` argument bind
to an overload that only takes `TIMESTAMPTZ_NS`, such as a `date_diff`
that mixes the two.

If that is acceptable, as a v2.0 regression, could this get the
`backport v2.0-cyanoptera` label?
subject: Compare TIMESTAMPTZ_NS with TIMESTAMPTZ without an explicit cast (#28672)
title: Compare TIMESTAMPTZ_NS with TIMESTAMPTZ without an explicit cast

author: Laurens Kuiper <laurens@ducklabs.com>
message:
Update the vendored moodycamel queue, blocking queue and semaphore to
[v1.0.5](https://github.com/cameron314/concurrentqueue/tree/9afb99746f0f5fc94ac8aef737053ae0481ba8d1),
and separate frequently written counters that otherwise share cache
lines.

* Import the upstream fixes, including memory-order corrections and
Linux monotonic semaphore timeouts.
* Add byte padding between producer/consumer counters and between the
semaphore count and OS semaphore, preserving ordinary alignment and
custom allocator support.
* Preserve DuckDB's namespace, scheduler observation APIs and TLS
destructor enqueueing behavior; add allocation, bulk reuse, move/swap
and thread-exit regression tests.

On a 192-core Graviton4, padding the refreshed headers improves
throughput by **2.55×** with one producer/191 consumers and **1.28×**
with 96 producers/96 consumers. Semaphore wake p95 falls by **6%**, with
**22% less CPU time**. These use five interleaved measurements per
variant.

For TPC-H SF100 at 192 threads, the complete change reduces summed query
medians by roughly **0.3%**: **0.31% and 0.33%** in opposite starting
orders. The upstream update alone changes the total by roughly **0.1%**.
All 22 queries used one warmup and five measured samples per variant,
with validated results.

Padding adds 112 bytes per producer and 120 bytes per semaphore on this
ARM machine, without increasing individual queue elements. The upstream
update also adopts its newer dynamic-block recycling policy and default
preallocation.

Validation: release and reldebug builds; 8,882 fast tests passed, 212
skipped; 2,711 focused assertions under ASan/UBSan; 18 concurrent
sanitizer checks at 8 and 192 threads. Independent review found no
remaining correctness or structural issues.

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
## Fixes #28562

### Root Cause Analysis
- **File:** `src/optimizer/rule/empty_needle_removal.cpp`
- **Function:** `EmptyNeedleRemovalRule::Apply`
- **Lines:** The optimisation rewrites `contains(<non‑string>, '')` to a
constant `TRUE` because it only checks the return type (`BOOLEAN`) and
the needle type, but **does not verify the type of the first argument**.
This violates the invariant that optimisation rules must preserve
semantics for all overloads.

### Surgical Solution & Edge‑Case Safety
The fix inserts a guard that ensures the first argument is of type
`VARCHAR` before applying the empty‑needle rewrite. If the first
argument is not a string (e.g., `LIST<VARCHAR>`), the rule aborts,
leaving the original expression untouched. This restores correct
behaviour for `contains(list, '')` while keeping the optimisation for
genuine string overloads.

### Verification
- Run the DuckDB test suite to ensure no regressions: `make test`.
- Add a new test case (if not already present) that checks `SELECT
contains(["a", ""], '')` returns `false` (or `null` for a null list) and
that the optimizer does not replace it with a constant.
- Verify that existing string‑optimisation tests still pass.

---
*No other files are modified.*

author: Laurens Kuiper <laurens@ducklabs.com>
hunk_contexts: static bool CastToVARIANT(Vector &source, Vector &result, idx_t count, CastParam
inline void VariantBuilderAppendBytes(string &blob, const_data_ptr_t data, idx_t
message:
Since #27782, the radix hash table finalize copies the row of a group
that is new to a partition instead of combining it into a fresh state.
For `histogram`, `mode` and `entropy`, the copied state keeps an
`OwningStringMap` that copies non-inlined strings into the arena of the
sink thread that created it. Several finalize threads then combine into
maps bound to that same arena. `ArenaAllocator` is not thread-safe, so
the maps end up with corrupted, duplicated or unsorted keys.

`ThreadSanitizer` report:
```
 WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race
   Write of size 8 by thread T95:
     #0 duckdb::ArenaAllocator::Allocate(unsigned long long) arena_allocator.hpp:79
     #2 duckdb::Allocator::AllocateData(unsigned long long) allocator.cpp:131
     #3 duckdb::OwningStringMap<...>::CopyString(duckdb::string_t) owning_string_map.hpp:119
     #7 duckdb::HistogramFunction<...>::Combine<...>(...) histogram.cpp:66
     #12 duckdb::GroupedAggregateHashTable::Combine(...) aggregate_hashtable.cpp:1256
     #13 duckdb::RadixHTLocalSourceState::Finalize(...) radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:1154
   Previous write of size 8 by thread T92: (same stack, another finalize thread)
   Location is heap block of size 56 allocated by thread T92:
     #2 duckdb::ArenaAllocator::AllocateNewBlock(unsigned long long) arena_allocator.cpp:86
     #10 duckdb::HistogramUpdateFunction<...>(...) histogram.cpp:112
     #15 duckdb::RadixPartitionedHashTable::Sink(...) radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:690
 SUMMARY: ThreadSanitizer: data race arena_allocator.hpp:79 in duckdb::ArenaAllocator::Allocate(unsigned long long)
```

The arena chunk was created by a sink thread (`HistogramUpdateFunction`)
and two finalize threads then allocate from it through
`OwningStringMap::CopyString`.

~~Combine now checks whether the target map copies its strings into the
caller's arena. If not, it rebuilds the map there before inserting and
deletes the old map. The old strings stay valid in their arena.~~

**EDIT** the fix moved one layer up, into
`GroupedAggregateHashTable::Combine`. States no longer change owner: a
new group still copies the source row (the group columns), but its
states are initialized fresh with the target table's allocator and the
source state is combined into it and destroyed, the same as for existing
groups. This covers every aggregate without per-aggregate code.
subject: Fix race on string histogram/mode/entropy states combined into reused rows (#28315)

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
Grammar extension transform functions only get the tokens and their byte
offsets, not the query they were cut from. The parser tokenizer drops
comments and whitespace, so a grammar extension that wants to keep part
of a statement exactly as it was written (e.g. the body of a definition
it stores, including comments) currently has no way to get at it, other
than a `parser_override` that reparses the whole query itself.

This makes the `TokenIterator`s that `Parser::ParseQuery` and
`ParseIterator` create point at the (normalized) query text they
tokenized. Transform functions can then use
`transformer.token_iterator.Source()` together with the offsets they
already have:

```cpp
auto open = list.GetChild(1).GetOffset().GetIndex() + 1;
auto close = list.GetChild(3).GetOffset().GetIndex();
auto body = transformer.token_iterator.Source()->substr(open, close - open);
```

`Source()` is null for iterators created without the text, like the ones
autocomplete uses, which only match and never transform.
subject: Let grammar extension transforms read the query text (#28377)

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
This adds a mode to the unittester that turns DuckDB warnings into
errors, plus a CI config run that uses it. Tests can then no longer
quietly rely on deprecated behavior such as the no-op `PRAGMA
enable_verification`.

### The mode
- New test config option `warnings_as_errors` (also available as
`--warnings-as-errors` / `--no-warnings-as-errors`). With it on, the
runner sets `logging_level='WARNING'`, `enable_logging=true` and
`warnings_as_errors=true` on every database it creates. That uses the
existing `warnings_as_errors` setting, so a statement that logs a
warning fails with the warning as its error:
  ```
  Query unexpectedly failed! (test/...:4)!
  PRAGMA enable_verification;
Invalid Input Error: The 'enable_verification' pragma no longer has any
effect; it is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
  ```
- `test/configs/warnings_as_errors.json` runs the suite in this mode. It
is added to `TEST_CONFIGS_QUERY_VERIFICATION`, so it runs in the "Linux
Config (Query Verification)" CI job.
- AGENTS.md now mentions the rule.

### Cleanups so the config passes
- Removed the no-op `PRAGMA enable/disable_verification` and
`enable/disable_object_cache` from 60 tests, along with comments that
explained them.
- Rewrote `PRAGMA name=value` to `SET name=value` in 796 tests. This is
a mechanical change in its own commit. Bare identifier values are
quoted, because `SET explain_output=all` does not parse while the PRAGMA
form converted identifiers to strings. Malformed PRAGMA lines that test
parser errors are left as they are. `pragma_assignment_deprecated.test`
still covers the deprecated form.
- Replaced implicit identifier-to-string conversions in about 20 tests
with string literals: bare type names in `columns=` / `hive_types=` /
`dtypes=`, double-quoted file paths, `format = auto`, and similar. `SHOW
t` / `SHOW (query)` are now `DESCRIBE`, and an unordered `OFFSET` now
has `ORDER BY rowid`.

### Engine fixes found by the new config
- **COPY `PARTITION_BY` warned for JSON/GeoJSON.** Formats that do not
register `copy_options` skipped the generic COPY option list, so
`PARTITION_BY (part)` with a bare column was treated as a deprecated
identifier conversion. Parquet was already exempt and tested. Added
`test/sql/json/copy_json_partition_by_identifier.test`.
- **`CALL enable_logging()` always warned that CLI warnings may be
lost**, even when it kept the shell's log storage or the shell was not
involved at all. It now warns only when it moves logging away from
`shell_log_storage`. A shell test covers the no-warning case.

### Skipped in this config (132 tests, grouped by reason in the JSON)
- Tests that check a warning on purpose, or the behavior with
`warnings_as_errors` off.
- Logging tests that rely on the default logging configuration, which
this config changes.
- Tests of deprecated settings: `lambda_syntax` (35), `profiling_mode`
(12), `delim_join_as_cte`, `error_on_division_by_zero`,
`*_metadata_reuse`, `old_implicit_casting`, `legacy_*`, and
`extension_directory` (9, which could migrate to `extension_directories`
in a follow-up).
- Views stored by older versions with the lambda arrow syntax.
- Tests whose queries apply `OFFSET` to an unordered input.
- **Possible false positive, needs a decision:** table macros such as
`histogram_values(tbl, col)`, `compute_top_k(...)` and
`query_table(tbl)` take table and column names as bare identifiers,
which the identifier-conversion deprecation warns about. Following the
warning's advice changes the result: `histogram_values('integers', 'i')`
bins the constant string `'i'` instead of column `i`. These 9 tests are
skipped instead of "fixed". The deprecation probably needs to exempt
table-macro parameters.

### Testing
- `build/reldebug/test/run --test-config
test/configs/warnings_as_errors.json`: 6123 passed, 0 failed (77 skipped
by `require`/`require-env`)
- `build/reldebug/test/run` (default, no config) after the rewrite: 8824
passed, 1 failed. The failure is `Test path canonicalization with
symlinks`, which fails only because I pointed `--temp-dir-root` at
`/dev/shm` on the shared box; it passes with the default temp dir
- Slow tests touched by the PRAGMA→SET rewrite: all 185 touched
`.test_slow` files run: 179 passed, 6 skipped by `require`
- Shell (`tools/shell/tests/test_warning.py`): pytest isn't installed on
the box I used, so I checked the two cases by hand with the CLI. `CALL
enable_logging(level='warning')` followed by `CALL
enable_logging(level='info', storage='shell_log_storage')` prints no
warning, and switching to `storage='file'` still prints it.
- `make format-fix` was not run (no clang-format/black available on that
box). The C++ and Python edits are small and follow the surrounding
style; the Code Quality check will catch anything off.
subject: Add a warnings_as_errors unittester mode and CI config run (#28493)

author: Laurens Kuiper <laurens@ducklabs.com>
hunk_contexts: void CommitState::CommitEntry(UndoFlags type, data_ptr_t data, CommitInfo &info)
message:
Split out of #27616: dropping a single overload member is useful for
plain macro overload sets and does not depend on extension-defined
function languages.

Macros support typed overload members, but DROP always removes the whole
entry. A parameter type list on DROP now names one member:

```sql
CREATE MACRO f(a INTEGER) AS a + 1, (a VARCHAR) AS a || '!', (a) AS 0;
DROP MACRO f(VARCHAR);
SELECT f(1);    -- 2, the INTEGER overload stays
DROP MACRO f(ANY);    -- names the untyped member
DROP MACRO f(INTEGER);    -- error: the last overload, drop the macro itself instead
DROP MACRO f;
```

A signature matches a member exactly: each type must equal the member's
declared parameter type, and `ANY` names an untyped slot. There is no
wildcard or compatibility matching, so a signature names at most one
member. Empty parentheses name the zero-parameter overload. The
signature's type names resolve against the schema of the entry the drop
found, so user types compare against the stored overload identity. IF
EXISTS applies at member granularity: a signature naming no member
succeeds without touching the siblings. The signature types bind like
any alter's types, so an unknown type name errors even under IF EXISTS
on a missing macro, as `ALTER TABLE IF EXISTS` does.

A signature drop is an ALTER from the parser on. The statement
transforms into an `AlterStatement` carrying `RemoveMacroOverloadInfo`
(`AlterType::ALTER_MACRO`), which renders back as the `DROP` statement.
It binds through the generic ALTER binder, which looks up a table macro
too when `DROP MACRO` finds no scalar macro, as the DROP binder does,
and executes through `CatalogSet::AlterEntry` and
`MacroCatalogEntry::AlterEntry` like any alter. The member removal keeps
the entry the same logical object with the same oid.

An alter keeps the entry, so a signature drop cannot remove the last
overload, just as `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN` cannot drop a table's
last column. Naming the last overload raises "Cannot drop the last
overload of f: drop the macro itself instead", and `DROP MACRO f` drops
it. This differs from PostgreSQL, where `DROP FUNCTION f(int)` on the
only overload drops the function. CASCADE never applies to a signature
drop: a dependent of the macro blocks the alter with the generic "Cannot
alter entry f because there are entries that depend on it", and only
dropping the macro cascades.

Dependencies stay registered per entry. A member drop keeps the entry's
whole dependency list, including what only the removed overload
referenced. This is conservative: such a dependency keeps blocking a
drop of what it references until the macro is dropped or recreated. It
never loses protection a surviving overload needs, adds no storage
fields, and only applies with `enable_macro_dependencies`, which is off
by default.

Racing member drops on one entry fail with the regular alter write-write
conflict, and a member drop rolls back like any alter. A member drop
that races the creation of a dependent is rejected in either commit
order. If the removal commits first, the creator's commit checks its own
snapshot for an overload that has since been removed. If the dependent
commits first, the removal runs the existing DROP commit check.
Otherwise either commit would succeed and leave a WAL that cannot be
replayed.

A member drop needs storage v2.1.0. Releases before v2.1.0 do not know
the `ALTER_MACRO` WAL record and would treat it as a torn WAL tail,
silently dropping every committed transaction after it. A database below
v2.1.0 therefore rejects a member drop, as it rejects macros with a
declared RETURNS type: "Dropping a single overload is only supported for
storage versions v2.1.0 and higher". TEMP macros and in-memory databases
are exempt. The default storage version is still v2.0.0, so a default
persistent database needs ATTACH with (STORAGE_VERSION v2.1.0) to drop
single overloads.

The concurrent-commit checks and their test come from Laurens Kuiper's
patch.

Tests are in `test/sql/catalog/function/`:

- `drop_function_signature.test`: exact matching, `ANY`, type modifiers,
quoted and user types, IF EXISTS, table macro members, built-in macros,
TEMP members, the last-overload rejection, CASCADE, write-write
conflicts.
- `drop_function_signature_dependencies.test`: kept dependencies,
dependent blocking.
- `drop_function_signature_persistence.test`: restart and checkpoint on
a v2.1.0 database, the rejection on a v1.4.0 database.
- `drop_function_signature_alter.test`: oid preservation, WAL replay,
the schema dependency, the last overload with dependents, the rejection
on v1.4.0 and v2.0.0 databases.
- `drop_function_signature_concurrent.test`: both commit orders,
including recovery, and harmless concurrent alters that still commit.
subject: Support DROP MACRO and DROP FUNCTION with a parameter type list (#27890)

author: Hannes Mühleisen <227792+hannes@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
## Problem

`enable_external_access=false` is meant to confine a connection to the
database itself, but `CREATE SECRET` was still reachable. Secret
providers are the place where external state enters the engine: the core
`env` provider copied `http_proxy*` from the process environment with a
bare `std::getenv`, extension providers (`credential_chain`, `config`
with file paths, ...) read config files and credential endpoints, and
persistent secrets write to the secret directory. Only the persistent
path was blocked, and only indirectly, through the file-system check
during secret-storage initialization; once the secret manager was
initialized, or with `allow_persistent_secrets=false`, every provider
worked as before.

## Fix

Secret creation through SQL is now refused as a whole once
`enable_external_access` is false, at a single choke point in the
`SecretManager`, so providers added by extensions are covered as well:

* `SecretManager::BindCreateSecret` throws `Permission Error: Creating
secrets is disabled when enable_external_access is false (secret type
"s3", provider "credential_chain")` before the secret storage is
initialized or the type is looked up, so no extension is autoloaded for
an unknown secret type and the error names the setting instead of a
file-system detail. The message carries the type and provider as written
(the provider is left out when the default is used), so it stays
informative and provider-specific tests keep matching.
* `SecretManager::CreateSecret` (the only entry point
`PhysicalCreateSecret` goes through) throws the same error, so a
statement prepared before the setting was disabled, or a direct API
caller, is refused at execution time as well.

This covers every provider (`config`, `env`, extension providers),
`TEMPORARY` and `PERSISTENT`, `CREATE OR REPLACE`, `IF NOT EXISTS` and
`IN <storage>`.

Left alone on purpose:

* `SecretManager::RegisterSecret` (the programmatic API that stores an
already-built secret, used by hosts and extensions without user SQL): it
reads no external state, and a host that locks SQL down with
`enable_external_access=false` may still want to configure secrets
itself, the same way the C API allows the database path.
* Reading, listing and dropping existing secrets: `duckdb_secrets()` and
`DROP SECRET` keep working on secrets that exist, and loading the
persistent secret directory keeps its existing file-system gate.

The `env` provider also keeps reading through `OSUtil::GetEnv` instead
of `std::getenv`, so it shares the environment-access gate (and the
Windows wide-char handling) with the shell's `getenv()` as defence in
depth.

## Tests

* `test/sql/secrets/create_secret_external_access.test`: creates a
temporary and a persistent secret, disables external access, and checks
that the config and env providers, `TEMPORARY`, `PERSISTENT`, `CREATE OR
REPLACE`, `IF NOT EXISTS`, `IN memory` and an unknown (extension) secret
type are all refused with the new message, while the secrets created
before remain listed with their values.
* `test/sql/settings/test_external_access_secrets.test`: now expects the
new message instead of the file-system error for `CREATE PERSISTENT
SECRET`.
*
`.github/patches/extensions/aws/0005-refuse-secret-creation-without-external-access.patch`:
the aws extension's `aws_credential_chain_external_access.test` asserted
that a `config` secret can still be created with external access
disabled; the patch turns that into the expected permission error (the
credential_chain expectations keep matching through the provider in the
message).

Note: this PR was generated by an AI coding agent and reviewed by the
author.
subject: Refuse CREATE SECRET when enable_external_access is false (#28637)

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
Continues moving `DBConfigOptions` / `ClientConfig` fields to generic
settings (stored in the user settings maps, read through
`Settings::Get<...>`).

Converted (field removed, setting is now generic):
- `abort_on_wal_failure` -> `debug_abort_on_wal_failure`
- `debug_order_verification`
- `checkpoint_on_shutdown` -> new global setting
`checkpoint_on_shutdown`; `PRAGMA enable/disable_checkpoint_on_shutdown`
now set it
- `force_checkpoint` -> new debug setting `debug_force_checkpoint`;
`PRAGMA force_checkpoint` sets it
- `trim_free_blocks` -> new setting `trim_free_blocks`
- `buffer_manager_track_eviction_timestamps` -> new setting
- `debug_initialize` -> new debug setting (enum)
- `ClientConfig::{enable_progress_bar, print_progress_bar, wait_time}`
-> `enable_progress_bar`, `enable_progress_bar_print`,
`progress_bar_time` (validation and `system_progress_bar_disable_reason`
check live in `OnSet`; setting `progress_bar_time` still enables the bar
and reset clears it)

Tests that assigned the old fields now use `SetOption`. `SET GLOBAL
enable_progress_bar` now reports the generic "cannot be set as a global
variable" error.

`checkpoint_on_shutdown`, `trim_free_blocks`, `debug_force_checkpoint`,
`debug_initialize`, `debug_abort_on_wal_failure` and
`buffer_manager_track_eviction_timestamps` are global-only, because
their readers use the `DBConfig`.
`buffer_manager_track_eviction_timestamps` can only be set in the
startup config. Setting the progress bar options on a `DBConfig` fails
with the global-option error, as before.

Visible introspection changes:
- `current_setting('debug_order_verification')` reports the enum name
(`CREATE_SORT_KEY`, default `NONE`) instead of lowercase.
- `duckdb_settings()` reports the scope of an unset session-only
progress setting as `GLOBAL`, since the value comes from its default.

Not converted (kept custom, need side effects or special parsing):
`checkpoint_threshold`, `custom_user_agent`, `force_mbedtls`,
`enable_block_allocator`, memory-limit style settings
(`max_streaming_buffer_size`, `operator_memory_limit`,
`write_buffer_row_group_memory_limit`), `verify_parallelism`
(pragma/`Connection` only), the profiling settings,
`variant_legacy_encoding`.

Tested locally: reset, progress bar, pragma, settings, WAL/checkpoint
and eviction tests pass (the only failure is
`reset_global_extension_option.test`, which needs the not-built demo
extension).
subject: Convert more DBConfig and ClientConfig options into generic settings (#28571)

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
A plan serialized by v1.x that calls `struct_update` runs incorrectly on
2.0. When it only updates existing fields, such as `struct_update(col, i
:= 10)`, it returns `col` unchanged without an error. When it also adds
a field, such as `struct_update(col, i := 10, j := 'x')`, it fails with
"INTERNAL Error: Attempted to access index 2 within vector of size 2".

v1.x resolved the field that every argument of `struct_update` writes
when the function ran, by matching the aliases of the arguments against
the field names of the struct, and only stored the result type. Since
#26844 the fields are resolved at bind time and kept in `field_indexes`
(property 101) of the bind data, which is all that execution reads.
Plans written by v1.x don't have that property, so `field_indexes`
deserialized as empty.

This PR rebuilds `field_indexes` from the argument aliases and the
result type when it is missing, the way v1.x resolved the fields.

The added plan cases we're serialized with 1.5
Could this still be backported?
subject: Keep the fields struct_update writes in plans serialized before v2.0.0 (#28653)
title: Keep the fields struct_update writes in plans serialized before v2.0.0
