message:
`ExpressionExecutor` now always has a `Context &`, so expressions can
use it instead of an optional client context.

- `ExpressionExecutor` takes a `Context &` (new constructors); the
`ClientContext &` constructors forward to `Services()`. A
`DatabaseInstance &` constructor covers callers without a client
(`BoundIndex`). The context-less constructors are removed.
- `ExpressionExecutor`/`ExpressionState`: `GetContext()` returns
`Context &`; new `GetClientContext()` (throws if there is no client) and
`TryGetClientContext()`; `HasContext()` is now `HasClientContext()`.
- `GetCastFunctionInput` takes a `Context &` (or `ClientContext &`);
`context` is now `client_context`, and `GetContext()` returns the
services. `VectorOperations::Cast`/`TryCast` gain `Context &` overloads,
and the executor's VARIANT verification cast always uses them.
- Expressions that only need services use `Context` now: string
decompression, crypto hash, adaptive filter logger, shell OS util, and a
few tests. The rest use `GetClientContext()`.

Limitation: the `Default*` cast helpers (`DefaultCast`, `DefaultCastAs`,
...) have no database, so they use `GetCastFunctionInput::Default()`,
whose `GetContext()` throws. Making that mandatory would require a
database for ~400 call sites.

Tested: `test/sql/cast`, `test/sql/function` and `[api]` pass (2 `[api]`
failures are `/dev/shm` temp-dir path issues). The full unittest run had
no failures related to this change; the 4 failures are environment
issues (missing loadable extension builds, temp-dir path, port in use)
or came from my own SIGTERM when I stopped a slow run.
subject: Make ExpressionExecutor take a mandatory Context (#28594)

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
Since 9c2cb27 (#20327), join predicates that reference both sides
without splitting into a left and right side (e.g. a + b < 1) are
combined
by JoinCondition::CreateExpression as AND(expression, condition), which
reverses the written order. A guard like a + b < 1 can then run after
get_bit and let it throw.

Build AND(condition, expression) so the conjuncts keep the written
order.

Fixes #28628
subject: fix(join-condition): keep the same execution order as written (#28645)
title: fix(join-condition): keep the same execution order as written

author: Mark <mark@ducklabs.com>
message:
Fix https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/27224

`SET active_grammar_extensions` replaces the list wholesale, so an
extension cannot enable its grammar without knowing which other grammar
extensions the client has turned on, and vice versa. In the CLI this
meant `SET active_grammar_extensions=['shell']` silently dropped any
grammar extension that activated itself from `OnConnectionOpened`, and a
user activating their own extension with `SET` lost bare-expression
statements.

This PR adds an append/remove form:
```
CALL add_grammar_extension('pipe_query_syntax');    -- appends, no-op if already active
CALL remove_grammar_extension('pipe_query_syntax'); -- removes, keeps the rest
FROM duckdb_grammar_extensions();          -- new `active` column
```

- Both functions go through `ActiveGrammarExtensionsSetting::SetLocal`,
so validation, lock_configuration and grammar caching are shared with
`SET`. Names are case insensitive. Unknown names raise an error with a
"Did you mean" suggestion.
- The CLI now runs `CALL add_grammar_extension('shell')` instead of the
SET, so extensions that activate themselves on the connection stay
active.
- `duckdb_grammar_extensions()` gains an active BOOLEAN column instead
of adding a separate list function.

```sql
DuckDB v2.0.0-dev88461 (Development Version, bde1b27b46)
Enter ".help" for usage hints.
memory D call duckdb_grammar_extensions();
┌─────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────┐
│  name   │                               description                               │ active  │
│ varchar │                                 varchar                                 │ boolean │
├─────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────┤
│ shell   │ Run a bare expression list or table name as a statement (CLI shorthand) │ true    │
└─────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴─────────┘
memory D call add_grammar_extension('duckpgq');
Invalid Input Error:
Grammar extension "duckpgq" does not exist
Did you mean: "shell"
memory D call remove_grammar_extension('duckpgq');
Invalid Input Error:
Grammar extension "duckpgq" does not exist
Did you mean: "shell"
memory D call remove_grammar_extension('shell');
┌─────────┐
│ Success │
│ boolean │
└─────────┘
  0 rows
memory D 1*1;
Parser Error:
syntax error at or near "1"

LINE 1: 1*1;
        ^
memory D select 1*1;
┌─────────┐
│ (1 * 1) │
│  int32  │
├─────────┤
│       1 │
└─────────┘
memory D call add_grammar_extension('shell');
┌─────────┐
│ Success │
│ boolean │
└─────────┘
  0 rows
memory D 1*1;
┌─────────┐
│ (1 * 1) │
│  int32  │
├─────────┤
│       1 │
└─────────┘
```

author: Hannes Mühleisen <227792+hannes@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
## Issue #27867

SUMMARIZE over the nanosecond temporal types added in 2.0 raised a
binder error:

SUMMARIZE generates \x60avg()\x60 and \x60approx_quantile(x, pos)\x60
for temporal columns, but neither function had overloads for
\x60TIMESTAMP_NS\x60, \x60TIMESTAMPTZ_NS\x60 or \x60TIME_NS\x60.

## Root cause

- \x60avg\x60: no overloads for the three \x60_NS\x60 temporal types.
\x60TIMESTAMP_NS\x60 only worked at all via a lossy implicit cast to
\x60TIMESTAMP\x60 (nanoseconds truncated to microseconds);
\x60TIMESTAMPTZ_NS\x60 and \x60TIME_NS\x60 did not bind at all.
- \x60approx_quantile\x60: the \x60INT64\x60 internal-type dispatch path
already handled these types, but they were never registered.

## Fix

- **avg.cpp**: add native \x60avg()\x60 overloads for
\x60TIMESTAMP_NS\x60, \x60TIMESTAMPTZ_NS\x60 and \x60TIME_NS\x60 using
\x60DiscreteAverageOperation\x60 (the same integer-rounding path as
\x60TIME\x60/\x60TIMESTAMP\x60), preserving nanosecond precision.
\x60TIME_NS\x60 gets a nanosecond state-import validator mirroring the
existing microsecond \x60ValidateTimeAverageStates\x60.
- **approximate_quantile.cpp**: register the three \x60_NS\x60 temporal
types for \x60approx_quantile(x, FLOAT)\x60 (the single-arg form
SUMMARIZE uses).

## Verification

- New regression test
\x60test/sql/show_select/test_summarize_temporal_ns.test\x60 (8
assertions) — passes.
- Existing suites all green: \x60test/sql/aggregate/*\x60 (232 cases,
258345 assertions), \x60*quantile*\x60 (24 cases), \x60*summarize*\x60
(6), \x60[show_select]\x60 (14), \x60temporal_avg.fuzz\60,
\x60test_time_ns.test\x60.

Note: \x60approx_quantile\x60 over \x60_NS\x60 types returns values with
sub-second precision limited by the 53-bit HLL sketch (pre-existing
property of the approximate function) — SUMMARIZE only requires it to
bind and return the correct type, which this provides. \x60avg\x60 is
exact.

Fixes #27867
subject: Fix: SUMMARIZE over nanosecond temporal types (TIMESTAMP_NS, TIME_NS, TIMESTAMPTZ_NS) (#27903)
title: Fix: SUMMARIZE over nanosecond temporal types (TIMESTAMP_NS, TIME_NS, TIMESTAMPTZ_NS)
